newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka police find guns at labour union office.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka police find guns at labour union office.

text.p: Sri Lankan police on Tuesday found 32 shotguns in an office of a labour union affiliated to a fringe left-wing political party, police said.
Police raided the offices of the union, which they said was affiliated to the Nava Sama Samaja Party (New Socialist Party), on a tip-off, a police officer who organised the raid told Reuters.
"The guns were well greased and wrapped in polythene and concealed in a specially-built compartment of brickwork and concrete under a staircase," he said.
Three party members were detained for questioning, he added.
A party spokesman denied that the guns belonged to party members or that the union had any relationship with the party.
But he confirmed that three party members had been arrested.

Police said they believed the guns were those issued by the former United National Party government to politicians for protection during an uprising by the left-wing Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna (People's Liberation Front) in 1988-90.
Tuesday's raid was carried out as part of a crackdown on unlicensed firearms.
